newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Opposition planes bomb Kabul airport.
newsitem.headline: Opposition planes bomb Kabul airport.

text.p: Opposition warplanes launched three air raids on Kabul overnight and on Wednesday morning, hitting the airport, but causing no casualties, witnesses said.
They said at least three bombs fell on the airport, in a northeastern district of the Afghan capital, damaging the apron and the terminal building, but leaving the runway intact.
Another bomb fell on waste ground inside the perimeter of the battered airport, used for military and civilian purposes.
"The runway is functioning and ready for flights," airport manager Mizbahullah Nuri told Reuters.
Opposition planes screamed twice over Kabul on Tuesday night and woke up residents again at 5.10 a.m. (0040 GMT). It was not immediately clear if bombs had hit other areas of the city.

The raids followed fighting north of Kabul last week that has forced thousands of civilians to flee their homes in areas captured by the Islamic Taleban militia from opposition forces led by General Abdul Rashid Dostum and Ahmad Shah Masood.
